terms.grammar: the genitive of gēns, beside the noun it describes; gentium of several peoples
terms.comment: Latin has no adjective for “ethnic”: it uses the people itself, gēns (see international), in the genitive, or the people’s own name (Graecus, Thrāx). An ethnic group is simply a gēns or a nātiō.

terms.grammar: the ablative of genus, with an adjective of nationality
evidence: Caes. BG 4.12.4: amplissimō genere nātus (Lewis & Short, s.v. genus)
terms.comment: Birth, descent: genere Atticus, Athenian by birth; also of family rank (nōbilī genere nātus).

evidence: Cic. Lael. 70: ignōrātiō stirpis et generis (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. minority (ethnic, religious, etc.): minor dīversae stirpis plēbs (Egger)
terms.comment: Literally the stock of a plant; of people, a family line. Egger’s ethnic minority is “people of a different stock”.
A false friend: in Latin, from Greek ἐθνικός, it means a heathen, a gentile (Tertullian, the Vulgate), not “ethnic”.

phrases.latin: erat is puer genere Atticus, ad annōs maximē nātus octō, fēstīvissimīs aetātis et gentis argūtiīs scatēns
phrases.english: the boy was an Athenian by birth, eight years old at most, bubbling over with all the wit of his age and of his people
